# Accessibility

4 rules in this category.

## accessibility-EADA4301

**MUST_NOT:** Never use color as the only visual distinction in an infographic.

*Colorblind and visually impaired users cannot decode meaning from color alone.*

Sources:
- https://www.nngroup.com/articles/designing-effective-infographics/

---

## accessibility-1365021E

**MUST:** Ensure content is readable in all browsers.

*Websites exist to deliver consumable content; readability across browsers honours that purpose.*

Movements: `brutalism`

Sources:
- https://brutalist-web.design/

---

## accessibility-FEBB9B60

**SHOULD:** Strive for clarity and accessibility rather than absolute perfection.

*Accessible clear presentation matters more than flawless execution on first pass.*

Sources:
- https://www.nngroup.com/articles/designing-effective-infographics/

---

## accessibility-F05C4757

**SHOULD:** Use HTML as intended so pages stay readable without custom styling.

*Semantic HTML defaults already support all screen sizes; custom design should not undermine that baseline.*

Movements: `brutalism`

Sources:
- https://brutalist-web.design/
